steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Thank you, Chief.
Are you fine with just that?

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Okay.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: You helped me meet my father and issue Ariel Spencer's obituary. I'm sure that has caused enough trouble for you already, Chief.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: I... don't know how to thank you.

options: It's not a big deal. You don't need to take it to heart.

choices.text: It's not a big deal. You don't need to take it to heart.

steps.content: You are standing in front of a brand new tombstone with the name "Ariel Spencer" engraved on it.
Looks like he still recognized you as a member of the family in the end.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: ...I see.
The new tomb is in a good location. It is at the back of the Spencers' garden, overlooking the funeral being held.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: My father... he's really stubborn and hard to change.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Like the majority of people in Eastside, he was hostile to Sinners.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: If I hadn't injured my father at that time... do you think he would've changed his opinion of me?
It's all in the past.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Yeah, it's all in the past.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Even if I could change my father, I'd not be able to change the prejudice of Eastside. I know.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Rather than adding to the family's worries, this is for the better.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Ariel was never allowed to meddle in the family's affairs. Now, I've managed to have a shared secret with my family.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: It's just that... Father would believe he had killed his daughter. Would he feel a sense of guilt?
Ariel looks at the distant funeral procession with a complex expression.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: I used this method to get my father's attention. I guess I also have a despicable side...

options: He may not care about you.

choices.text: He may not care about you.

steps.content: He humiliated you so much before and even shot at you.
You're nothing compared to the selfishness and ruthlessness of Ganson.
... Since I learned the real purpose of your return, I realized that you are not so innocent and naïve as I imagined. You are smarter than I thought.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Huh...? So you always thought I was silly, Chief?
I've never seen anyone blatantly save a Maniac.
But then again, I also need to apologize to you.
Many of the Sinners are criminals. After hearing your confession, I was not totally convinced.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Did you suspect me, Chief?
You did not sense it in the interrogation room?

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: I-I was too nervous back then...

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: I thought that you would believe me if I were truthful...
Ah, a little naïve indeed...
As you're chatting, the funeral procession is moving slowly from the estate to the cemetery.
You can't let them see you. We should go now.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Okay.
Ariel looks toward the Spencers' estate for the last time, her eyes filled with sentiment as if she wanted to engrave the scene in her memory forever.
After what feels like an eternity—or a second, you don't know—she turns and smiles at you.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Let's go... home.
The evening wind ruffles her bangs, her eyes glistening.
She called it... home. This word gives you mixed feelings.
Do you regret saving that person?

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: No, I don't.
Then do you regret leaving behind the extravagant life of the Spencer family?
She traces her finger gently over the surname on the tomb. The last rays of twilight dance on the dark gray stele and her fingertips.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: No, I don't.
You're not sure if it is her ability or her benevolence that makes her look so beautiful and holy in the sunset.
The silent prayer of the young girl's heart is gone with the wind and melts in the boundless night.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: This needs to avoid light... So it's best to place it here.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Hmm... This one needs to be stored at a low temperature, so we have to put it in the freezer.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Freezer... freezer...
Ariel walks toward the freezer with her eyes looking downwards, not noticing that you're standing in front of it.

options: Let me help you place it.

choices.text: Let me help you place it.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Thank you... huh?

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Chief? Why are you here?
I came to see how you've been doing lately.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Please don't worry. Ever since entering the medical team, Ariel has grown a lot.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Look, I'm helping with the classification and preservation of medications.
Uhh... but the bottle in your hand doesn't need to be stored at a low temperature.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Ah... you're right.
Ariel fumbles to identify the potion's label. Maybe she still has a way to go before "growing a lot."
Why don't you start with some easier work? It might be safer and more tolerant.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Trust me, Chief, I can do it... This goes here, right?
It looks like she won't stop until she's done something, so you decide to leave her be.
By the way, I came with good news for you.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Good news?
It's about Shan.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Who's that?
The girl you helped get away in Eastside. We found her in Syndicate.
Her M value shows no signs of increasing for now, and she's already started a new life.

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Really?! That's great! I really helped her!
She smiles and breathes a sigh of relief as she puts the potion in her hand into the freezer.
(Crack)

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Did you hear that, Chief?
Seems like a sound of a test tube cracking?

steps.speaker: Ariel
steps.content: Oh no! This one can't be stored at low temperatures, either!
